text: Almu is an Irish goddess. She was honored in the eastern province Leinster, on the Hill of Allen. The hill was once the sacred capital of the province. The regional kings ruled from it. The hill carried the name Almu, a word that means all-white. The name also described the royal citadel on the hill's crest. An unseen entrance to the Otherworld was said to sit on the hill. The Otherworldly king Nuad owned it at first. The hero Fionn mac Cumhaill won it from him by strength of arms. The hill is often named as the birthplace of Fionn. His chair, a small mound, sat at the summit. Many confuse Almu with Dún Ailinne or Knockaulin, near Kilcullen. That hill was the older home of the kings of Leinster.
objective: Record Almu, an Irish goddess of the Hill of Allen.
